memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And this is what he sent to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the best things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other provisions for his journey. Then he sent his brothers away, and as they were leaving he said to them, 'Don't quarrel on the way!'" — Gen 45:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a very human, very wise parting word. "Don't quarrel on the way!"

Joseph knows exactly what is coming. Somewhere on that long road home, one brother is going to say, "This is your fault — you suggested selling him." And another will say, "You held the rope." Old blame will come out. Forgiven people can still tear each other apart over a settled past.

So Joseph heads it off before it starts. I have forgiven you. Do not spend the journey home punishing each other for what I have already dealt with.

The church needs this word constantly. We can accept God's forgiveness in theory and still carry grudges, still keep score, still relitigate old failures with one another. But if God has forgiven a matter, who are we to keep it open?

Paul's instruction to believers is exactly this: "Forgive as the Lord forgave you" (Col 3:13). Not more strictly. Not with conditions He never attached. The same way.

Whatever is behind you and settled at the cross — let it be settled between you and others too. The journey is long enough without carrying old quarrels the whole way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an old matter you keep reopening with someone?
2. Do you forgive others in the same way God has forgiven you?
3. What quarrel is God asking you to put down today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have settled my sin completely at the cross. Help me stop reopening what You have closed, both in my own heart and with others. Give me peace on the journey. Amen.
